title: ‘American Idol’ Contestant Caleb Flynn Receives Maximum Sentence for Wife’s Murder
summary: The musical pastor was given life in prison without the possibility of parole.
contentText:
Caleb Flynn, the former American Idol contestant who was found guilty of murdering his wife, Ashley Flynn, has been sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.

The musical pastor received his sentence in court on Monday (Oct. 5), six days after an Ohio court determined he was guilty on all charges spanning aggravated murder and multiple counts of murder, felonious assault and tampering with evidence in connection with the death of Ashley, with whom he shares two young daughters. He was given the maximum possible sentence for his crime.

Additionally, Caleb was sentenced to two mandatory three-year prison terms for gun specifications.

Caleb had pleaded not guilty leading up to the trial and, when given the chance on Monday to share remarks for the first time in the entirety of the court proceedings, reasserted his innocence in the death of Ashley. He did, however, apologize to his former in-laws for being unfaithful to his wife and for the “awful and hurtful” things he said about her in texts to Alleigha Botner, with whom he had an affair for 1.5 years and often talked to about wanting Ashley to die.

The church leader’s correspondence with Botner — who was 21 when she met Caleb and, now 24, delivered hours of testimony during the trial — was key in the prosecutors’ case against him in terms of establishing motive. “If I could literally kill her and not go to hell, I would do it in a heartbeat,” he texted Botner of Ashley in May 2025, according to CNN . “That’s how dark and hateful I feel.”

Texts used as evidence in the trial also showed that on Feb. 15, Caleb told Botner that he was planning to inform Ashley he was leaving her the following day. Instead, the next day marked Ashley’s last, as first responders arrived at the family’s Tipp County home and found her dead via gunshot. At the time, Caleb had called 911 and claimed that an intruder had broken in and killed Ashley.

Caleb visibly shook and shed heavy tears as he stood before the court Monday, dressed in an orange jumpsuit with his hands cuffed. In between his remarks and the judge’s reading of his sentence, Ashley’s friends and family read aloud victim impact statements, including two penned by the Flynns’ daughters, who were not present.

“Dear Daddy, I don’t even know where to start,” began the letter written by Caleb’s daughter Ava, as read to the court by Matt Keyt, who is now raising the girls alongside his wife, Ashley’s sister Kayla. “How could you do such a thing? I looked up to you. I loved you with all of my heart, and then you lied to everyone. Mommy was the perfect person — the absolute perfect person. What did she ever do to make you hate her so much?”

As read by Ashley’s mother, Jill, Alyssa Flynn wrote to her father: “By the way, I don’t plan on coming to see you.”

Caleb competed in the 12th season of American Idol in 2013, making it as far as the televised judges’ auditions but not advancing to the main competition. “I love to sing, so that’s why I auditioned — and my wife kind of nudged me a little bit too,” he said in his “Road to Hollywood” interview at the time. “I love my wife more than anything. She is very, very pretty.”
